entries.subject: Published phase curves as a map of longitude (TESS, Patel et al. 2025; CHEOPS, Deline et al. 2022)
entries.finding: Read on 2026-10-08. Patel et al. (2025, arXiv:2512.05175) fit the TESS curve with a first-order Fourier series (E 203.4 ppm, C1 137.8, D1 -23.6), but its night-side flux is negative (-71.8 +36.4/-36.0 ppm), so the map has no night side to check, and the printed day and night temperatures (2746 and 1529 K) are hemisphere means of the paper's own two-dimensional map, not brightness temperatures of the fitted depth. Deline et al. (2022, arXiv:2201.04518) fit CHEOPS with a reflecting sphere plus a thermal sinusoid whose split the paper calls degenerate, with the night flux fixed at zero. Neither prints what the published phase-curve reader needs.
entries.revisitWhen: A paper prints a day-side and a night-side brightness temperature of one band from a first-order fit, or releases its map as a file.
